Data Processing, Integration, and Clustering

Chomchon Uansiri

Source: vignettes/OHMmy-processing-clustering.Rmd
OHMmy-processing-clustering.Rmd

Introduction

Once your single-cell RNA-seq data has been quality-controlled and decontaminated (e.g., via SoupX), the next major steps are Normalization, Batch Integration, and Clustering.

OHMmy provides highly automated wrappers built on top of Seurat v5 to handle these complex steps seamlessly. Our pipeline automatically manages technical variable regression (like cell cycle or mitochondrial percentage), handles variable V(D)J receptor gene exclusion, integrates batches, and systematically evaluates cluster resolutions.

Part 1: Loading and Preparing the Data

First, we load our cleaned Seurat object. If you are re-analyzing an object that has already been processed, you can optionally clear out the old reductions and scaled data to start fresh.


library(Seurat)
library(OHMmy)

# 1. Load the quality-controlled Seurat object
seurat_obj <- readRDS("data/seurat_qc_filtered.rds")

# Optional: Clean old reductions if re-processing an existing object
seurat_obj <- CleanSeuratReductions(seurat_obj)
seurat_obj[["RNA"]]@layers[["scale.data"]] <- NULL

Part 2: Normalization and Batch Integration

We use the ProcessSeuratLOG() wrapper to perform standard Log-Normalization, identify highly variable features, scale the data, and run PCA.

Crucially, this function allows you to:

  • Regress out technical noise (e.g., mitochondrial/ribosomal percentages, cell cycle scores).

  • Exclude TCR/BCR genes from highly variable features so clustering is driven by cell phenotype, not clonotype (tcr_bcr_patterns).

  • Automatically run your preferred integration method (CCAIntegration, HarmonyIntegration, RPCAIntegration, or FastMNNIntegration) across your batches.


# Process, Regress, and Integrate (e.g., using CCA)
seurat_integrated <- ProcessSeuratLOG(
  seurat_obj,
  batch_col = "batch",
  
  # Variables to regress out during scaling
  vars_to_regress = c(
    "pct_counts_mt", "nCount_RNA", "percent.ribo", 
    "S.Score", "G2M.Score", "percent.ig"
  ),
  
  # Prevent TCR/BCR genes from driving clustering
  tcr_bcr_patterns = "^TR[ABDG]|^IG[HKL]", 
  
  # PCA and Integration settings
  dims = 1:40,
  reduction_name = "pca.log",
  integration_method = "CCAIntegration",
  integration_reduction = "integrated.cca.log",
  
  interactive_mode = FALSE
) 

# Save the integrated object
saveRDS(seurat_integrated, file = "results/seurat_integrated_cca.rds")

Part 3: Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering

Finding the optimal clustering resolution can be tedious. OHMmy’s ClusterAndUMAP() function automates the creation of nearest-neighbor graphs, runs clustering across a wide sequence of resolutions, generates a clustree plot to help you track cluster stability, and calculates the UMAP coordinates.


# Run UMAP and test clustering across multiple resolutions
cluster_results <- ClusterAndUMAP(
  seurat_obj = seurat_integrated,
  
  # Use the integrated reduction from the previous step
  reduction = "integrated.cca.log",
  dims = 1:40,
  
  # Naming conventions
  umap_name = "umap.cca",
  graph_name = "log.cca_snn",
  cluster_prefix = "log.cca_snn_res.",
  
  # Sequence of resolutions to test (0.1 to 2.0)
  cluster_resolutions = seq(0.1, 2, by = 0.1),
  final_resolution = 1.0, # The default resolution to set as active identity
  
  # Advanced parameters
  k.param = 600,
  force_neighbors = TRUE,
  force_clustering = TRUE,
  
  # Output settings for the Clustree plot and automated saving
  sample_name = "Sample_Cohort", 
  plot_dir = "results/plots/",
  save_path = "results/seurat_final_clustered.rds"
)

# Extract the fully processed Seurat object
seurat_final <- cluster_results$seurat

# View the final object with new UMAP and Cluster metadata
seurat_final

After this step, your results/plots/ directory will contain a helpful clustree visualization showing how clusters split and evolve as the resolution increases. Your Seurat object is now fully prepared for Differential Expression testing and functional enrichment!
